changes.summary: `extractReleaseArtifact` names the entry it refuses (`Release artifact contains an unsafe entry: <tar listing line>`), so a rejected archive says what to leave out

`extractReleaseArtifact` takes `excludeNames`: bare names left out at any depth, neither extracted nor held to the safety check, so an archive whose producer shipped a dependency tree's symlinks can still be received

changes.detail: `InfrastructureNode` gains `size` (slug, vCPUs, memory, disk, hourly and monthly price in integer micros) and `createdAt`, filled by the DigitalOcean fleet provider. Providers may expose `billing`: `listInvoices` (final invoices and the open month's preview) and `listInvoiceLines` (per-resource lines with the provider's resource id, span and amount in micros). DigitalOcean implements it; its line fingerprints match Management's DigitalOcean import so both name a line identically. `amountToMicros` converts decimal currency strings exactly.
changes.summary: Nodes report their billed size and providers can read the account's bill (DigitalOcean)

changes.detail: DigitalOcean stops offering regular sizes in busy regions without notice and then rejects new droplets with `422 Size is not available in this region`, even though droplets of that size already run there. Droplet creation (`digitalOceanTarget`, the fleet provider, and the new `createDigitalOceanDroplet`) now retries once with the cheapest size offered in that region that has at least the requested vCPUs, memory and disk, and reports the swap through `onSizeSubstitute` (a console warning by default). Any other failure, and a region with no such size, still fails with DigitalOcean's reason. `equivalentDigitalOceanSize` exposes the choice.
changes.summary: A droplet whose size the region stops offering is created at the cheapest at-least-as-large size instead

changes.detail: A failed DigitalOcean API call's error message now ends with DigitalOcean's own reason, for example `... failed: 422 Unprocessable Entity: creating this/these droplet(s) will exceed your droplet limit`. It used to stop at the status line, which left callers guessing. An error body that is not JSON is kept as text on `DigitalOceanError.body` instead of throwing a JSON parse error.
changes.summary: DigitalOcean API errors name DigitalOcean's reason

createReleaseArtifact takes excludeNames: file names (globs allowed) left out wherever they occur, such as .env or .env.*. Paths in exclude are anchored to the source root, and BusyBox tar's * does not cross /, so a nested credential file could not be excluded before; an owner-only one made the whole archive fail.
Trusted native certification accepts a bounded portable Sigstore bundle and full workflow identity before retaining provenance
Native release registries retain content-addressed acceptance certification and optional trusted provenance with channel promotion
Expo staged-rollout pause, resume, cancellation, and fleet fallback transitions receive stable activation identities so installed apps can select the trusted server state.
